title: Overselling races and checkout edges
idea: Overselling happens when two buyers both read "one left" and both take it; the fix makes reading and decrementing stock one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two shoppers see one cake in the window and both run in. A ticket machine at the door hands out the only ticket once.
analogy.breaks: A real machine queues people; a failed CAS must retry or give up.

points: Check-then-act is two steps, so another buyer can act in between.
`compareAndSet` writes only if the count is still what you read.
An Idempotency-Key makes a retried checkout return the same order.
Reservations carry a deadline; a sweeper frees stock that nobody paid for.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. One T-shirt is left in stock.
U-7 reads the count: one left, so it plans to buy.
Before U-7 writes, U-9 reads the same count. Both believe they can buy.
U-7 decrements and reports a sale. Stock is now zero.
U-9 acts on its stale read and decrements too. Two sales, one shirt.
Safe version. Both threads ask `compareAndSet` to move the count from 1 to 0.
Only one swap can see 1. U-7's swap succeeds and the count becomes 0.
U-9's swap fails. It rereads, sees zero, and reports out of stock.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier makes both buyers read before either writes, so the oversell happens on every run.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: unsafe first, then with compare-and-set.
One unit in stock, a barrier for two threads, and a sales counter.
Safe: wait for both, then try an atomic reserve.
Unsafe: both read one left, wait for each other, then both decrement.
Join both threads before reading the counts, so output is stable.
The CAS loop: refuse if too few, swap if unchanged, else retry.

code.title: Edge cases in checkout
code.caption: Changed prices, retried requests, declined cards and abandoned orders, with time passed in so every run is the same.

walk.text: The price rose after the cart was shown. The shopper confirms, then retries.
Key k-2 takes the last mug as OR-2; OR-1 pays on a second try; OR-2 is abandoned.
A known Idempotency-Key returns the stored order and reserves nothing new.
Refuse if the total differs from what the shopper saw, or stock is short.
Reserve stock and give the order a fifteen-minute payment window.
Pay refuses closed or late orders. A declined card keeps the hold until the deadline.
The sweeper cancels unpaid orders past their deadline and releases stock.

pitfalls: Never read stock, then write it, in two separate steps; use one atomic operation.
Reserve multi-item carts in sorted SKU order, or two checkouts can deadlock.
If a payment lands after the order was cancelled, refund it; never resurrect the order.

quiz.q: What is the first line StockRace prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads read one left before either writes. Both then decrement and count a sale: two sold, minus one left.

takeaway: Make check and decrement one atomic step; give every reservation a deadline.

starters: Why does AtomicInteger not prevent the first race by itself?
Should a declined card release the reservation straight away?
What happens to in-memory reservations if the server restarts?
